chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Buraed ibn Muhammad al-Ghadiri, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw me, and I was wearing black sandals. So he said: 'O Ubayd, what is it with you and the black sandals? Do you not know that in them are three characteristics: they slacken the manhood, weaken the vision, and they are more expensive in price than others. And indeed, a man wears them while he possesses only enough for his family and children, so Allah resurrects him as a tyrant.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of black sandals mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the specific practice of wearing black sandals to three distinct effects: physical weakening of virility and eyesight, and economic extravagance. The hadith emphasizes the spiritual danger of ostentation, warning that a man who wears them while financially constrained—possessing only enough for his family—will be resurrected as a 'jabbar' (tyrant or oppressor), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that external adornment can manifest internal arrogance and social injustice.
